content.title: Women’s Final Four live updates: How to watch, time, channel for UConn vs. USC, UCLA vs. Texas
content.text: South Carolina and UCLA will play for the women's college basketball national championship Sunday, after both won in the NCAA Tournament's Final Four on Friday. UCLA is making its first national championship appearance in program history, while South Carolina will play for a title for the fifth time since 2017. UCLA held off a late charge by Texas to win, 51-44, behind 16 points from star center Lauren Betts, who also grabbed 11 rebounds and blocked three shots, including a crucial block in the final minute to keep the Bruins in control.South Carolina advanced after dethroning the tournament's No. 1 overall seed, Connecticut, 62-48, in a game that snapped the Huskies' 54-game winning streak that began 476 days earlier. Dawn Staley is in her 18th season leading the Gamecocks and will be looking for her fourth championship as a head coach.The Huskies won last season’s national championship against the Gamecocks, but South Carolina exacted revenge this year. It was an ugly, defensive-slugfest of a game, as the Gamecocks shot only 38% from the field. But four different players scored in at least double digits, led by Ta’Niya Latson’s 16.The Huskies got a baffling performance from their best players, however. Senior guard Azzi Fudd and Sarah Strong, two of the top players in the sport, were held in check offensively. Fudd and Strong combined to score 20 points and shoot only 22.6% from the field.Officiating was also a storyline. Connecticut head coach Geno Auriemma complained about the referees after the third quarter, telling ESPN’s Holly Rowe during a mid-game interview the free-throw disparity was “ridiculous.” Strong also seemed frustrated, tearing her jersey after a non-call at the end of the third. The Gamecocks shot 22 free throws, compared to only 6 for the Huskies. Before walking off the floor, Auriemma got into a heated exchange with Staley near halfcourt and the two had to be separated. Staley said she had “no idea” why Auriemma was so upset. More Sports from NBC News South Carolina players then watched from the stands in Phoenix to see which opponent then would face Sunday. Texas scored just 28 points through three quarters against UCLA, fell behind, 45-32, with 4:36 left in regulation, and appeared on its way to losing, when the Longhorns suddenly awoke offensively. During a three-minute stretch, they outscored UCLA, 12-2, to cut its deficit to just 47-44. With 20 seconds left in regulation, Texas All-American Madison Booker tried to cut the lead to just one, but her driving layup attempt was blocked by UCLA star Lauren Betts. Down five points in the final seconds, Texas tried to make one last rally when Booker had a chance at a layup, only to stumble before she could take a shot. It continued the worst offensive performance of the season for Booker, the typical engine of the Longhorns’ offense. She made three of her 23 shot attempts, at one point missing 17 consecutive shots, and didn’t attempt a free throw. 12d ago / 11:59 PM EDT“I think it was rugby more than basketball” - Cori CloseUCLA coach Cori Close apologized to fans on ESPN after her team’s Final Four win, joking about the defensive slugfest everybody just witnessed.Close will certainly take the win, no matter how ugly it was. 12d ago / 11:52 PM EDTWhat a game!UCLA holds off a late comeback attempt by Texas, winning a white-knuckle defensive thriller to advance to the national title game.In a matchup between two teams who lost in last year’s semifinals, the Bruins beat Texas and now will have a chance for redemption. UCLA will play South Carolina — last year’s runner up — in the championship game on Sunday. 12d ago / 11:45 PM EDTBetts denies Booker!Wow!!!After a miss on the offensive end for UCLA, Texas forward Madison Booker zipped down the court and tried to hit a layup, but she was blocked by UCLA's Lauren Betts.The Bruins still lead 47-44 with 18 seconds to go. 12d ago / 11:43 PM EDTUCLA is playing with fireTexas is on a 12-2 run and this is now a three-point game with 55.8 seconds to go. 47-44 UCLA. 12d ago / 11:35 PM EDTTexas shows life after UCLA takes 13-point leadUCLA was up 45-32 with about four minutes to play in regulation and Texas looked done. The Longhorns had shot 16-of-56 from the field, including 1-of-8 on 3-pointers, and had scored seven points combined on free throws and fast-break opportunities. But then the Longhorns scored five consecutive points, and suddenly UCLA's lead doesn't feel so insurmountable. The Bruins only lead 45-37 with 3:35 to play in the fourth quarter.12d ago / 11:28 PM EDTHow bad has the offense been tonight?UCLA is shooting 38% from the field, 25% from three, and has 18 turnovers compared to only 11 assists... and the Bruins are winning the game!Texas has been even worse, shooting 27% from the field, 13% from 3-point range, and 33% from the free-throw line for good measure. 12d ago / 11:23 PM EDTRori Harmon has gone coldAfter carrying Texas in the first half, Rori Harmon has now gone cold.Harmon started the game shooting 4-of-6 from the field for 8 points, but she’s missed her last four shots and hasn’t scored since the first half. 12d ago / 11:22 PM EDTUCLA pushes lead to 10 in fourth quarterThe Bruins have their second double-digit lead of this game. Not since the first quarter has their lead over Texas been as large as it is now, up 38-28 with 8:30 to play in the fourth quarter.Kiki Rice hit a 25-foot 3-pointer, then Gabriela Jaquez made a fastbreak layup off of a Texas turnover. Considering how difficult it has been for both teams to score tonight, this 10-point lead feels twice as large. ESPN's win probability has UCLA at 93.9%.12d ago / 11:14 PM EDTEntering fourth quarter: UCLA 31, Texas 28Will the first team to 40 points win? Texas is shooting 14-for-48, while UCLA has made 13 of its 37 shots. UCLA led by as many as 10 points in the first half but it has been a taut game throughout the second half. 12d ago / 11:07 PM EDTOffense has all come inside the paintIn this third quarter, neither team has made a field goal outside of the paint. Both Texas and UCLA are 0-for-3 from outside the paint in the quarter.UCLA leads, 29-26, with under 1 minute to play in the third quarter.12d ago / 11:01 PM EDTMiserable night for Madison BookerMadison Booker’s Final Four struggles continue.After Booker had a disappointing 11-point game in the Longhorns’ Final Four loss last season, she’s on pace for an even worse effort tonight. Through nearly three quarters, Booker has only 2 points on a ghastly 1-of-16 shooting. Clearly bothered by UCLA’s size, Booker has missed 14 straight shots. 12d ago / 10:58 PM EDTUCLA leads, 26-21, midway through third quarterLauren Betts now has eight points, to go with seven rebounds, to keep the Bruins slightly ahead with five minutes to play in the third quarter. Both teams are shooting worse than 40%.12d ago / 10:58 PM EDTA better start for Texas in the second halfAfter shooting only 8-of-32 as a team in the first half, the Longhorns are 2-of-4 to start the third quarter, and have hit their first 3-pointer of the night. The Bruins still lead by 5, however. 12d ago / 10:52 PM EDTUCLA star Betts hits head on courtLauren Betts, UCLA's leading scorer, tumbled to the floor when she collided with a Texas's Madison Booker with 7:19 to play in the third quarter. Betts hit the back of her head on the court when she fell. Referees are now examining the play.12d ago / 10:41 PM EDTThe second half is underwayUCLA leads, 20-17, as the third quarter begins of this national semifinal from Phoenix.The winner will meet South Carolina in Sunday's national title game.12d ago / 10:28 PM EDTHalftime: UCLA 20, Texas 17Just as UConn and South Carolina were held well below their season averages for offense during the first semifinal, UCLA and Texas have been in a defensive slog to start their game. Both these teams average around 85 points per game and, barring a significant change in the second half, will be held well below those marks.The headline so far is that Madison Booker, the All-American Texas star, has missed 11 consecutive shots. 12d ago / 10:27 PM EDTIt’s been a one-woman show for the LonghornsTexas has to be ecstatic to be down only 3 points at halftime, and it has senior guard Rori Harmon largely to thank. Harmon has 8 points on 4-of-6 shooting at the break. The rest of her teammates have combined for 9 points on 4-of-26 shooting. Junior forward Madison Booker, the team’s leading scorer entering tonight, has made only 1-of-12 shots for 2 points. If the Longhorns complete this comeback, Harmon’s first half can’t be forgotten. 12d ago / 10:20 PM EDTOne more note on UConn and South CarolinaRemember the heated exchange between Dawn Staley and Geno Auriemma after the Gamecocks upset the Huskies?Here’s what Auriemma said about it postgame:“I said what I said, and obviously she didn’t like it. I just told the truth.”12d ago / 10:18 PM EDTTexas awakensThe Longhorns have pulled within 18-15 with four minutes left before halftime after jumpers by Rori Harmon and Aaliyah Crump. Their star teammate Madison Booker has missed 10 consecutive shots, meanwhile.12d ago / 10:14 PM EDTWatch: timely block by UCLA's Angela DugalicDugalic blocked the Texas' Ashton Judd and then appeared to stare her down a bit. The Bruins' defense has been stout early in this one.12d ago / 10:11 PM EDTUCLA continues to hold lead in second quarterWith Texas star Madison Booker making just one of her first nine shots, the Longhorns remain stuck offensively, and trail UCLA, 16-8, with about 7 minutes to play in the second quarter.12d ago / 10:06 PM EDTThe ugly numbers on Texas’s cold startNot a pretty first quarter for the Longhorns, who shot only 3 of 14 for 21% shooting from the field. Madison Booker is 1-for-6, including 0-for-2 from 3-point range. Texas has also yet to get to the free-throw line.The result? The Longhorns scored 6 points in 10 minutes. 12d ago / 10:03 PM EDTEnd of first quarter: UCLA leads Texas 14-6The Bruins lead 14-6 after one quarter in the national semifinal, holding Texas to a season-low six first-quarter points.The Longhorns went five minutes between their second and third field goals. 12d ago / 9:54 PM EDTTexas faces largest deficit of NCAA TournamentUCLA's 12-4 lead with about 2 minutes to play in the first quarter placed the Longhorns in their largest deficit of this tournament — and then it got even bigger after a driving layup by UCLA that extended its lead to 14-4 with 2:08 left.UCLA is outrebounding Texas, 10-4.12d ago / 9:53 PM EDTNothing going for the LonghornsTexas has made only 2-of-9 field goals, and trails 14-4, its largest deficit of the tournament. 12d ago / 9:46 PM EDTUCLA finding its footing, takes early leadIn the face of an aggressive Texas defense, UCLA has settled in offensively, shooting 4-of-8 from the floor early. 12d ago / 9:46 PM EDTUCLA 9, Texas 4 early in first quarterThe Bruins already have taken three 3-point attempts in the first four-plus minutes of the opening quarter, while Texas has been content to work the ball in closer to the basket. 12d ago / 9:38 PM EDTUCLA-Texas is just minutes from tipping offThe night's second semifinal is just minutes away, with the winner of Texas-UCLA meeting South Carolina for the national championship on Sunday.Both UCLA and Texas are No. 1 seeds in this tournament.12d ago / 9:22 PM EDTWatch: Geno Auriemma exchanges words with Dawn StaleyIn the closing seconds of a loss that denied UConn a chance to win a second consecutive national championship, and ended the school's 54-game winning streak, Huskies coach Geno Auriemma began arguing with South Carolina coach Dawn Staley, who looked taken aback by the exchange. Auriemma would later leave the court without shaking hands of the opposing coaches, while Staley would defender her integrity in a postgame interview.12d ago / 9:12 PM EDT“I’m of integrity” - Dawn StaleySouth Carolina coach Dawn Staley said she was not sure what UConn coach Geno Auriemma was mad about when the two had a heated exchange toward the end of Friday's game. Staley claimed the UConn coach could be upset about the lack of a pregame handshake, but that she tried to find Auriemma before the game. 12d ago / 9:07 PM EDTFinal: South Carolina 62, Connecticut 48Before the handshake line could start, UConn coach Geno Auriemma got into it with his South Carolina counterpart, Dawn Staley, in a scene you rarely see even in the ultra-intense setting of a Final Four.The moment followed a stunning loss for UConn, 62-48, that ended a 54-game winning streak.Auriemma walked back to the Huskies' locker room by himself without shaking Staley's hand.12d ago / 9:04 PM EDTSouth Carolina pushes lead to 15 in final minuteThe Gamecocks will be headed to the national championship game for a third consecutive season.With 30 seconds left, South Carolina is blowing out UConn, 62-47, having held its stars, Sarah Strong and Azzi Fudd, in check all game. 12d ago / 8:58 PM EDTStunning defensive performance by South Carolina has it on the verge of a winUConn has averaged 87.9 points per game this season, yet with 1:45 to play in regulation, it trails, 57-47. UConn averages 52% shooting; today, it's made 32% of its shots.12d ago / 8:54 PM EDTSarah Strong scores first points of second halfThe AP Player of the Year in women's college basketball hasn't been heard from much since the first quarter. Her 3-pointer with about 4 minutes to go in regulation gave Strong her first points of the second half. But it still hasn't cut the gap. After another Strong miss, South Carolina leads, 53-47, with 3:25 to play.12d ago / 8:50 PM EDTNot the expected recipe for an upsetYou might think a team would have to play perfect to beat Connecticut and end its 54-game winning streak, but South Carolina not only has 14 turnovers, but Madina Okot, who averages 13 points per game, has just 4 points on only four shots. South Carolina also has shot poorly outside of the paint, making just four shots. And yet, UConn has looked so unsure of itself that it has opened the door for a potential loss.12d ago / 8:49 PM EDTGamecocks lead 51-44 in the fourth quarterWow!A deep 3-pointer from Agot Makeer gives South Carolina a 7-point lead with 5:53 left in the fourth quarter. Makeer has 12 points on 4-of-7 shooting, including 2-of-2 from 3-point range. 12d ago / 8:46 PM EDTFourteen turnovers now for the Gamecocks...South Carolina is going to have trouble holding on to win this game if it can’t take care of the ball. 12d ago / 8:41 PM EDTSouth Carolina's upset hopes could come down to free throwsPart of why UConn's Geno Auriemma just went on his rant on officials after the third quarter was because of the free-throw disparity.South Carolina is shooting 11-for-14 tonight from the free-throw line, while UConn is just 1-for-2. 12d ago / 8:39 PM EDT‘This is ridiculous!’ - Geno AuriemmaA furious Geno Auriemma went in on the referees after the third quarter, telling ESPN’s Holly Rower he was upset with the officiating. He implied Dawn Staley got away with a technical while he hasn’t been heard for his complaints.Sarah Strong also showed frustration, ripping her jersey after the end of the quarter. She’s now wearing a replacement jersey with a new number: 55. 12d ago / 8:36 PM EDTWe're about to see UConn's resolveFor just about every other team in all of college basketball, men's or women's, a 10-point deficit would be a run-of-the-mill occurrence, but UConn has been so rarely challenged during is unbeaten season that it makes me wonder how the Huskies will respond on such a high-pressure stage. The deficit isn't dire, but because they've so rarely trailed, will it lead UConn to panic? ESPN's Holly Rowe noted during a first-half report that coach Geno Auriemma instructed his team to take a deep breath during the opening quarter.The Huskies have already cut the lead to 5 points, entering the fourth quarter.12d ago / 8:35 PM EDTEnd of third quarter: South Carolina 44, UConn 39What a finish to the quarter!The Huskies caught fire from deep, hitting three straight triples to cut the lead to 1. But the Gamecocks scored the final four points of the third, taking a 5-point advantage into the final frame.We should be in for a fantastic finish. 12d ago / 8:31 PM EDTHere come the Huskies!Back-to-back-to-back 3-pointers and the Gamecocks’ 10-point lead has been cut to 1. 12d ago / 8:28 PM EDTTerrible shooting nights from UConn’s biggest starsSarah Strong and Azzi Fudd have combined to shoot only 4-of-20 from the field after another miss from Strong just now. The duo has only 10 points, perhaps the biggest reason the Gamecocks are winning. 12d ago / 8:25 PM EDTGamecocks staying in front in third quarterSouth Carolina leads 38-30 with 4:16 left in the third quarter. The Huskies are not used to playing from behind. Do they have to composure to make a comeback? 12d ago / 8:20 PM EDTUConn is back on its heelsConnecticut was so overpowering to start this NCAA Tournament that it had trailed for just shy of eight minutes combined during its first four games of March Madness. The Huskies have played from behind by that much in the first half alone tonight, and have spent virtually the entire third quarter also digging themselves out of a hole. South Carolina is only shooting 35% from the field and has 10 turnovers, yet UConn hasn't been able to take advantage, with eight of its own turnovers while also shooting 1-for-11 on 3-pointers.12d ago / 8:19 PM EDTLargest deficit of the season for the HuskiesThe Gamecocks lead 36-28, and the 8-point deficit is the largest that UConn has faced this season. There's 5:25 left in the third. 12d ago / 8:16 PM EDT8-2 run for the GamecocksSouth Carolina is up 32-28 about four minutes into the third quarter. 12d ago / 8:12 PM EDTSecond half is underway!UConn leads, but is coming off its lowest scoring half of the season. 12d ago / 8:04 PM EDTAzzi Fudd has yet to get on trackFudd, UConn's All-American senior, is 1-for-6 from the field and has yet to make a 3-pointer (0-4) during a first half where the Huskies lead, but have had to work so hard to do it. Fudd's 3-point shooting is the most surprising part. She led the Big East in 3-point accuracy each of the past two seasons, with a mark of 45.5% this season. Fudd has scored in the double digits in 35 games this season.12d ago / 7:59 PM EDTWho remembers the key stats we told you about?Extra possessions were always going to be key in tonight’s game, something you may recall if you’re a keen observer of our newsletter, The Sports Desk. (Click here to subscribe.)The Gamecocks are shooting only 31% and have nine turnovers, but have managed to stay close because of their work on the boards, collecting 10 offensive rebounds. Joyce Edwards and Madina Okot have been eating glass, combining for 10 rebounds in the first half.The Huskies, meanwhile, are doing a great job of getting out on the break. UConn has 6 steals, which have helped lead to 10 points off turnovers. 12d ago / 7:56 PM EDTHalftime: UConn 26, South Carolina 24A defensive slugfest between two of the best offensive teams in the country in the first half.The Gamecocks led by as many as 5 in the second quarter, but the Huskies closed on a 10-3 run to take a lead into the break. 12d ago / 7:51 PM EDTThis is no blowout, and Deebo Samuel is loving itFormer Gamecocks football star Deebo Samuel is in attendance at the Final Four to watch South Carolina pushing Connecticut like few opponents have tested the Huskies this season.UConn is 1-of-6 on 3-pointers so far, and has struggled mightily to shoot outside of the paint.12d ago / 7:47 PM EDTHuskies back in frontUConn is on an 8-2 run and leads 24-23 with 2:08 left in the first half. 12d ago / 7:43 PM EDTShade providing UConn with scoringImpressive outing for Ashlynn Shade of UConn so far, who has matched her NCAA tournament scoring average already with six points. With South Carolina set on trying to disrupt Sarah Strong and Azzi Fudd, their Huskies teammates will be needed to produce.12d ago / 7:43 PM EDTSouth Carolina 21, UConn 20The Huskies have scored 4 straight to cut into deficit. There’s 4:28 left in the second quarter. 12d ago / 7:39 PM EDTThe Gamecocks have their largest lead......And it’s 5 points. South Carolina is up 21-16 nearly four minutes into the second quarter. The Gamecocks are on a 11-1 scoring run.12d ago / 7:34 PM EDTWill UConn finally get tested? We've already told you about UConn's 54-game winning streak, which ties for fourth-longest all-time in Division I history. But that number, while eye-popping, somehow doesn't even tell the full story of UConn's dominance: During that winning streak, UConn has won by double-digits 53 times. South Carolina is trying to become the exception. One minute into the second quarter, it's still a tied game at 15-all. 12d ago / 7:32 PM EDTAn extremely fast startThat first quarter took about 18 minutes of real time, thanks to only two fouls being called — both on UConn's Blanca Quinonez. That isn't to say it has been an entirely clean start. South Carolina already has five turnovers.12d ago / 7:29 PM EDTEnd of first quarter: South Carolina 15, UConn 15We have a tied game after one quarter. The Huskies got out to an early lead before the Gamecocks finished the period on a little run.South Carolina is shooting only 40%, but has overcome the shooting woes by grabbing four offensive rebounds. 12d ago / 7:24 PM EDTUConn has had upper hand in rivalry of lateThis was the first season in 11 years that Connecticut and South Carolina did not play one another in the regular season, meaning that this Huskies-Gamecocks rivalry has a long history. In the last 10 meetings each team has won five times, but that's slightly misleading. South Carolina won four in a row between 2021-22 and 2023-24, but UConn won both meetings last season, including the national championship game.12d ago / 7:21 PM EDTHuskies out to an early leadUConn leads 13-8 with 3:27 left in the first quarter. The Huskies are shooting 50% from the floor, compared to 44% for the Gamecocks. 12d ago / 7:19 PM EDTSarah Strong showing why she is AP player of the yearUConn's superb sophomore already has five points in the first four minutes of this semifinal, including a 3-pointer. She's made nearly 41% of her 3-pointers this season, a bump from the 38% she shot as a freshman.12d ago / 7:16 PM EDTIt’s been a tight startNearly five minutes into the first quarter, the Huskies lead 9-4. These teams both averaged over 85 points per game entering tonight, and we’re far off that pace so far. 12d ago / 7:11 PM EDTWe’re off!The Gamecocks won the tip and quickly take a 2-0 lead. 12d ago / 7:04 PM EDTWe’re minutes from tipoff!A titanic showdown is about to take place momentarily, as a rematch of last year’s title game is minutes from tipping off. UConn and South Carolina enter with a combined record of 73-3. 12d ago / 6:56 PM EDTUCLA-Texas predictionOf the Final Four teams, UCLA is the only one that didn’t dominate its Elite Eight matchup. UCLA actually trailed Duke by eight points at halftime. Maybe that’s a sign the Bruins are vulnerable. Texas beat Michigan, its Elite Eight opponent, by 36 points. The Longhorns won the first matchup between these two teams, and they’ll take the sequel, too. Texas 70, UCLA 65.12d ago / 6:52 PM EDTUConn-South Carolina predictionIt’s going to be hard to pick against the Huskies. While both teams have great offenses, UConn also dominated defensively this season, leading college basketball in points allowed and opponent field-goal percentage. The Gamecocks will have to wait for revenge. Huskies win, 88-70.12d ago / 6:44 PM EDTWhy is UCLA so difficult to beat?The Bruins force opponents to maximize every possession. UCLA owns the second-highest field goal percentage in the country this season (51.3%) and also grabs nearly 15 rebounds more than its opponents on average, meaning that if an opponent doesn't grab an offensive rebound for a second-chance opportunity, UCLA regularly goes downcourt and scores its own bucket to widen its lead.Lauren Betts, a candidate for the Wooden Award given to the country's top player, is vital on both ends. Betts is averaging 17.2 points and 8.6 rebounds and two blocks per game. Having played in the Final Four last year has helped this season, the Bruins said."I keep saying this, but we just have the mentality of this being a business trip," Angela Dugalic said. "And I honestly can’t emphasize that enough." 12d ago / 6:25 PM EDTStrong, Fudd are two-headed attackAll-Americans Sarah Strong and Azzi Fudd won a national championship last season and are key reasons why UConn could win another.Strong is one of college basketball's two-way stars by scoring a team-best 18.6 points per game while also averaging 3.4 steals per game. Named the Most Valuable Player of UConn's tournament regional, Strong is shooting 59% this season. "There is a level of confidence that Sarah has that I think she lifts (her teammates) up to someplace where they wouldn’t be able to be by themselves or with maybe somebody different," UConn coach Geno Auriemma said."So they play with confidence knowing they have her, and that’s probably the best compliment that I can give her, give Sarah."Fudd also is averaging more than 2.5 steals per game — remarkably, she and Strong are two of four Huskies averaging at least two steals. Fudd is also UConn's greatest threat from deep, shooting 45% on 3-pointers.12d ago / 6:16 PM EDTTexas looks for edge on UCLA again in Final FourNatalie Esquire, Terrika Foster-Brasby and Nicole Auerbach analyze the matchup between UCLA and Texas after the Longhorns handed the Bruins their only loss of this season.12d ago / 6:05 PM EDTHuskies' historic streak buildsUConn's victory in the Elite Eight against Notre Dame was the program's 54th consecutive win dating to last season, a streak that ranks among the longest in NCAA women's basketball history. The all-time record was 111 games, set by UConn between 2014-17. It also rattled off 90 straight wins from 2008-10 and 70 straight wins from 2001-03. The Huskies' current streak is tied for Louisiana Tech — which won 54 consecutive from 1980-82 — as the fourth-longest in Division I history. 12d ago / 5:55 PM EDTUCLA coach learned from John WoodenWell before she became UCLA's coach in 2011, Cori Close was already steeped in Bruins history through hours she spent with the iconic UCLA coach John Wooden.They met every Tuesday for several years, Bill Plaschke wrote in the Los Angeles Times last year, when Close would make a pilgrimage to Wooden's home starting when she was a young Bruins assistant. She kept in touch with Wooden, who was six decades her senior, as she moved up the coaching ladder."I tried to maneuver it, whatever I was doing, whatever off days I had, I tried to make quality time with him a priority, totally selfish on my part,” Close told the paper. “I would literally schedule my flights into LAX around going to see him. And amazingly, he always made time for me.”12d ago / 5:45 PM EDTUConn worth a play on spread vs. South CarolinaVaughn Dalzell and Trysta Krick dive into some of the best bets for the upcoming Final Four match between UConn and South Carolina, detailing why you should take the Huskies to cover the spread.12d ago / 5:35 PM EDTUConn women's and men's teams back in Final FourFor the sixth time, both the men's and women's teams at Connecticut made their respective Final Fours this season. Nine other schools have combined to do that nine other times in Division I history. Of the six times that UConn has had both its men's and women's teams in the national semifinals, it has swept both championships twice — in 2004, and 2014. 12d ago / 5:25 PM EDTKey matchup for UCLA-TexasThe way UCLA operates, Lauren Betts is the center of the Bruins’ universe, surrounded by four dynamic guards. Betts stands 6-foot-7 and is a force in the paint, and few college basketball teams can match her height. But Texas might be able to. The Longhorns start 6-foot-4 forward Breya Cunningham and bring 6-foot-6 center Kyla Oldacre off the bench. When these two teams played earlier this season, Betts had an uncharacteristically bad game — 8 points and 7 rebounds in 37 minutes.12d ago / 5:14 PM EDTSouth Carolina's sixth consecutive Final FourStarting in 2021, the Gamecocks have played in every Final Four, six straight in all (this is coach Dawn Staley's eighth Final Four overall). South Carolina has played in each of the last two championship games, winning in 2024.12d ago / 5:04 PM EDTTake the under in total points for Texas vs. UCLAVaughn Dalzell and Trysta Krick unpack some of the best bets for the upcoming Final Four clash between Texas and UCLA, analyzing why you should take the under in total points.12d ago / 4:55 PM EDTConnecticut's unbeaten dream continuesThe Huskies are attempting to become one of only a handful of teams in NCAA history to finish undefeated. Remarkably, Connecticut has done it six times previously under coach Geno Auriemma.2024: South Carolina (38-0)2016: Connecticut (38-0)2014: Connecticut (40-0)2012: Baylor (40-0)2010: Connecticut (39-0)2009: Connecticut (39-0)2002: Connecticut (39-0)1998: Tennessee (39-0)1995: Connecticut (35-0)1986: Texas (34-0)12d ago / 4:41 PM EDTLonghorns' top threat is Madison BookerShe wears No. 35 for Texas like Kevin Durant, and is similarly the Longhorns' offensive engine. Booker, the 6-foot-1 All-American, is averaging a team-high 19.3 points, 2.2 steals, 3.8 assists and 6.7 rebounds. 12d ago / 4:30 PM EDTGeno Auriemma on UConn hoops: 'We are a pro franchise'Before the Final Four, UConn coach Geno Auriemma was asked about the recent announcement that the WNBA's Connecticut Sun would be re-locating to Houston."So we don’t have a WNBA team," Auriemma said, "we don’t have an NBA team, we don’t have a Major League Baseball team, we don’t have an NFL, we don’t have an NHL team, but we have UConn basketball. "Maybe that’s why this is the sixth time that our men and women have been in a Final Four at the same time. ‘Cause we are a pro franchise, you know? We’ve always been a pro franchise."12d ago / 4:19 PM EDTRare halftime deficit sparks UCLA rally to reach Final FourFacing Duke in the Elite Eight, UCLA trailed at halftime for only the second time this season. The eight-point deficit wasn't enough, however, to keep the Bruins out of the Final Four. By the end of the third quarter, they led by four and never trailed again.At halftime, "I think we were just we were able to call each other up and out on like what we have to fix," UCLA's Angela Dugalic said after the win against Duke. "And I think that's a great quality of our team is no one takes it personally."12d ago / 4:11 PM EDTNCAA women's basketball talent gap may be widening"The Dan Le Batard Show" examines how the best women's basketball teams have separated themselves from the rest of the country and how NIL has played a role.12d ago / 4:00 PM EDTUConn isn't just winning. It's dominating.It's not uncommon for women's college basketball to be heavily stratified — a massive gap between the top teams and everyone else chasing them.
